name: Quest 1014 'Arugal Must Die': the turn-in buff reaching the Wondrous Wisdomball is the stock party-radius buff rule, not a targeting defect (#5795)
contract: quest_template.sql:1146 quest 1014 'Arugal Must Die' has RewardDisplaySpell (column 16) = 0 and RewardSpell (column 17, cast at turn-in) = 1460 Arcane Intellect - the reporter's screenshot names the correct spell, but an earlier triage pass read the wrong column. PlayerQuest.cpp's RewardQuest (GetRewSpellCast() branch) has the quest-giver creature CastSpell(player, 1460, true) because Arcane Intellect is not self-cast, teaches nothing and creates no item. Spell 1460's own Spell.dbc row (unmodified from Blizzard) sets EffectImplicitTargetA=TARGET_UNIT_TARGET_ALLY and EffectImplicitTargetB=TARGET_UNIT_SRC_AREA_PARTY on both of its APPLY_AURA effects: this is a party-radius buff by design, matching every Fortitude/Intellect-style reward flavor cast. Spell.cpp's TARGET_CHECK_PARTY filter (WorldObjectSpellTargetCheck::operator(), case TARGET_CHECK_PARTY) requires Unit::IsInPartyWith, which returns true whenever GetCharmerOrOwnerOrSelf() resolves both units to the same owner (Unit.cpp, u1 == u2). AscensionWisdomball.cpp's ActiveBall() itself keys the ball to the player through creature->GetOwnerGUID() == player->GetGUID(), so the summoned ball resolves to the player's own identity exactly like a hunter or warlock pet would. The companion picking up the reward buff is therefore the same stock AzerothCore/Blizzard party-buff-radius rule that sweeps any owned pet into a nearby Fortitude/Intellect cast - established, intended behavior, not a CoA quest-reward targeting bug.
